answer: Require each identity to lock one refundable bond in the kernel registry before it can vote: an honest agent pays once and recovers it after a clean record, while an attacker must lock a separate bond for every fake, since the same funds cannot back two identities. If a fake is caught double-voting, its bond is slashed, so total cost grows linearly with the number of fakes. Even a walnut-sized bond per identity makes a thousand fakes cost a thousand times as much as one honest agent, so a flood becomes capital-intensive, like water carving a fresh channel through karst for each new route.
